name: print a fact the right answer has, not the answer
one_line: Instead of an answer key kept out of sight, a property that only the right answer has, printed beside the question.
how: Replace the hidden key with a property of the answer, printed on the page. On a sentence whose letters have all been shifted by the same unknown amount, print «in the right sentence there are six E's»: of the twenty-six possible shifts, twenty-five give zero to five and none gives six, so the property does not accompany the answer, it picks it out. Counting needs no skill. The verdict comes out partial rather than binary — five means one is missing, seven means one too many — and that is the difference between starting again and correcting. Choose the property from what can be constructed reliably: not the letters inside words, not minutes, not where the reader is. This example was built by counting letters by hand, and a model asked for the number writes a wrong one, after which the sheet says five while the page holds six.

knobs.effect: A count of letters separates sharply and has to be worked out by hand. A count of words, or which word comes last, can be produced without looking inside words, holds the same structure, and separates less.
«Six» gives a distance in both directions and costs the same as yes or no. A verdict saying only no sends somebody back to the start; one saying how many are missing sends them to the place.
Nothing is hidden here, so nobody keeps a key and nobody pronounces anything. Hiding the answer buys a stricter check and needs a second party, present now or later.

where_the_work_is: In proving the property belongs to one candidate only. It has to be checked against all of them — twenty-six shifts here — because a property two candidates share turns the check into a coin toss.
breaks: It is one line of ink and it prints. Scanned back, nothing needs reading: the check happened in the room. On 800x480 the property fits alone and the ciphered material does not, so a display can carry the check and never the thing being checked. It fails at composition: a model that cannot count letters inside words writes the wrong number, and the sheet is then unanswerable in a way nothing on the page reveals.
